items.note: The focused filter field takes the spec's 2px blue border and a clear ×. It sits beside an ink 'All' pill with its white dot, and the count reads 'Showing 1 of 8', so the result of the query is plain. Above it are a row of four saturated stat tiles with cream pictogram plates and cream panels; the pieces match references 08 and 09. The stat figures (about 32px) are smaller than reference 08's dominant number.

Navy page, indigo panels, white pills with ink labels, and a yellow ring on the focused filter field. This is a convincing night palette in the spirit of reference 03. The bright white footer bottom bar still breaks the dark page at the end.

The focused filter field and its × read clearly further down the page. But the first screen is four full-width saturated stat slabs stacked one under another, so two or three fields share each viewport. Reference 04 keeps one yellow field per phone screen, and reference 08 sets its tiles in a row.

One sample tints the hovered row cream and underlines its title, which is the spec's quiet hover. In the other two samples the table looks unchanged, because titles are already underlined links and the row gets no tone. The state is much less designed than the reference's carefully drawn hover (reference 11).
Indigo table on a navy panel with blue round row-action circles. The hovered row is barely or not at all distinguishable from the rest, and the white footer bar remains.

Hover has little meaning on a phone. The table scrolls in its cream frame with the first column visible, but the screen again opens with four stacked full-width saturated tiles rather than the reference's single field.

The focus ring is a 2px blue outline with an offset that follows the pill shape, on the top-bar Search pill or a sidebar nav pill. It closely matches the focus-visible frame in reference 11 and is easy to spot.

At night the focused sidebar pill gets a yellow, pill-shaped ring that is clearly visible on indigo. This follows the spec's on-field ring and reads well. The white bottom bar remains at the page end.

The blue pill ring on the menu circle, search field or nav pill is clear and on-system. The rest of the first screen is still the stack of saturated tiles, which is cruder than the single-field phone layout in reference 04.

A white rounded menu with a float shadow drops from the cream user pill. It shows the email as muted meta, then three plain items. It is quiet and correct for the system's menus but has no item hover, and sign-out is not set apart.

The menu turns indigo with white items over the navy page and stays consistent with the night palette. It is legible, but it has the same flat list with no separation for sign-out, and the white footer bar remains.
The menu opens as a white card over the greeting and covers the title, which is acceptable for a menu. Below it, the stacked saturated tiles again fill the phone screen with several fields at once.

A white panel inside the cream projects card holds a flat folder-and-magnifier pictogram with a sparkle, an h4 'no match' title, one line of help and an ink 'Clear filters' pill. This follows the spec's no-results recipe exactly. The drawing is crisp, though flatter than the crescent-shaded plates in reference 07.
The same composition sits on an indigo panel with a white pill. The pictogram's hues hold on navy and the state reads clearly; the white footer bar is the one jarring surface.
The empty state itself scales down well: centered pictogram, wrapped title, full pill. It sits under the long stack of saturated tiles, so a person must scroll far past them to reach the result.

The Refresh pill keeps its width and shows pop dots with 'Loading metrics' text, and the stat tiles become cream skeleton blocks. Both follow the spec. In one sample the skeleton bars overlap one another inside each tile, which looks broken.
Indigo skeleton tiles, white pop-dots pill and loading text, all calm and on-system at night. The white bottom bar remains.

The phone shows the pop-dots pill with 'Loading' text and four cream skeleton tiles. Because the skeletons replace the saturated slabs, this is the calmest phone first screen of the set and closer to reference 04's restraint.

The greeting has one breathing glyph (zigzag, target or crescent with a sparkle). Each stat tile has a cream plate holding a flat crescent-shaded pictogram (rocket, bell, clock, hourglass, heart, sun-and-cloud) with a small sparkle. They are readable at a glance, each is its own drawing, and they are close to the spot plates in reference 07, if slightly smaller in their plates.

The blue header band holds a yellow folder with a darker back flap, a crescent-shaded orange or pink disc, a white cloud and four-point sparkles. It is well crafted and on-recipe like reference 02's band art. Its layout (lead centered, disc behind the upper right, cloud low right, star upper left) repeats on every area band.

An orange clipboard with a checklist, a second-hue disc cutting behind it, a cloud and sparkles on the blue band. The subject is right and cleanly drawn, but it uses the same silhouette and placement as the projects and team clusters.

Two overlapping crescent-shaded people figures in yellow and pink or orange on a green band, with a cloud and stars. Avatar discs carry initials with a lower-right crescent. The pieces are clear, faceless and on-system, but the band repeats the shared cluster layout.

The greeting glyph breathes on a 6s infinite scale-and-rotate loop with the slow easing. Stat-tile plates fade in once over 500ms, and data appears immediately. This matches the calm, slow motion the spec describes.

findings.summary: On phones the dashboard stat tiles stack as four full-width saturated slabs, about 170px each, so the first two screens show two or three large colour fields at once. The figure in each is small for its tile, and the data below is pushed far down. The reference keeps one saturated field per phone screen (04) and sets its stat tiles as a compact row (08), so colour reads as confidence rather than noise.
findings.promptFix: Stat tiles are one saturated field as a group, at every width. Below `breakpoint.md` they do not stack full width: lay them out as a 2×2 grid, or as one row that scrolls sideways, each tile about 120px tall. Keep the eyebrow, the big number and the caption, and move the plate beside the number or drop it. The whole group must fit in at most half of the first phone screen, so the next content starts in view.
findings.specRule: Below `breakpoint.md`: … card grids to one column (two below `breakpoint.lg`)

findings.summary: Every night page still ends in a bright white bottom bar under the indigo footer. It is the only light surface on the dark page; reference 03 stays dark to the edge. This was named in rc.3 and rc.4 review 1 and is still open.
findings.promptFix: Give the footer bottom bar its own role token, the darkest surface in both appearances: ink by day, and at night a step darker than the navy page, with white text. Keep `surface.inverse` for small floating pieces such as toasts.
findings.specRule: Footer | Cream band with rise arc, link columns, a signup field + ink pill; `surface.inverse` bottom bar with round icon buttons

findings.summary: In two of three samples the hovered project row shows no change. The table rows open their item through a title link and a circle action, so agents treat them as not clickable and give them no hover tone; the hover state then looks undesigned beside the reference's crafted states (11).

The header-band clusters for projects, a project's detail and the team all use one arrangement: the lead shape centered, a disc behind its upper right, a cloud low right and a star upper left. Only the lead subject changes. The spec asks for each area's own silhouette; the reference varies its compositions (02, 06, 07).
In one sample the stat-tile skeleton bars overlap one another inside each loading tile. This is an agent layout slip; the spec's skeleton guidance does not cause it.
